cards.hint: Think about the fixed share mentioned for every paycheck
options: 10 percent of what you earn
5 percent of what you earn
14 percent of what you earn
cards.quote: A good rule to live by is to save 10 percent of what you earn, and have at least three months’ worth of living expenses saved up
cards.stem: What portion of earnings is the basic saving guideline

cards.hint: Recall the starting point for covering living costs
options: three months’ worth of expenses
six months’ worth of expenses
nine months’ worth of expenses
cards.quote: Talk about how to estimate three months’ worth of expenses, and how much to save from each paycheck to build up their savings.
cards.stem: How far ahead should teens learn to estimate expenses for emergencies

cards.hint: Think beyond the minimum for extra safety
options: six to nine months’ worth of living expenses
a single paycheck of living expenses
only spare change of living expenses
cards.quote: Explain that, if possible, it’s better to have more savings—like six to nine months’ worth of living expenses, instead of only three.
cards.stem: If possible, what larger cushion is described as better for emergencies

cards.hint: Consider costly borrowing choices during a crisis
options: avoid having to rely on credit cards or loan options
lock money away with no access until retirement
spend all earnings on fun each month
cards.quote: can help your child avoid having to rely on credit cards or loan options that charge a high interest rate in case of emergency.
cards.stem: Why keep emergency money readily available in savings
